title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening Economic Trial Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Strengthening Economic Adjudication Work

Fa (Yan) Fa [1985] No. 28

To all local people's courts at various levels, all military courts, railway运输 courts, and all maritime courts:

The "Proposal of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Formulating the Seventh Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development," adopted at the National Conference of the Communist Party of China, points out: "The deepening of economic system reform and the further development of the national economy require that more economic relations and norms of economic activities be fixed in legal form, making law an important means of regulating economic relations and economic activities," and calls for attention to and strengthening of economic judicial work. To implement the spirit of the National Conference of the Communist Party of China, to safeguard and promote the smooth progress of the socialist economic system reform, and to better serve the construction of socialist material civilization and spiritual civilization, the following notice is hereby issued on several issues concerning the current further strengthening of economic adjudication work:

1. Regarding the Scope of Cases Accepted by People's Courts for Economic Adjudication

In March 1984, the First National Conference on Economic Adjudication Work clearly stipulated that the scope of cases accepted by people's courts for economic adjudication mainly includes: (1) Economic contract dispute cases, including economic contract disputes between legal persons, and between legal persons and individual business operators, specialized households, and rural commune members; (2) Foreign-related and Hong Kong/Macao-related economic, trade, transport, and maritime dispute cases; (3) Rural contract dispute cases; (4) Damage compensation dispute cases arising from tortious acts between legal persons or with a legal person as one party in the fields of production and circulation; (5) Economic administrative cases where a party, dissatisfied with an administrative sanction decision made by an administrative organ, initiates a lawsuit in a people's court in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) and relevant laws and regulations; (6) Other economic dispute cases between legal persons or with a legal person as one party that laws and regulations stipulate may be brought to a people's court.

In November 1984, this Court, in the "Decision on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of Maritime Courts," stipulated that the scope of cases accepted by maritime courts includes: 18 types of maritime and maritime cases, such as vessel collision damage compensation,海上 cargo transport, maritime salvage and assistance, and general average, which arise between domestic enterprises, organizations, and citizens, between Chinese enterprises, organizations, and citizens and foreign enterprises, organizations, and citizens, and between foreign enterprises, organizations, and citizens, and which are subject to the jurisdiction of Chinese courts according to law.

In May 1985, this Court, in the "Notice on Several Issues Concerning the Conduct of Patent Adjudication Work," specifically stipulated seven categories of patent dispute cases that should be tried by people's courts.

People's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the above provisions, promptly accept the various types of economic dispute cases listed above.

2. Seriously Study New Situations and Properly Handle New Problems

With the deepening of urban and rural economic system reform and the further implementation of the policies of opening up to the outside world and invigorating the domestic economy, new things are emerging in an endless stream in economic life, and economic dispute cases have multiplied, with more types and complex circumstances. Many of these are unfamiliar to us, and the law has not yet provided for them. In order to effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens, safeguard the interests of the state and collectives, and safeguard and promote the smooth progress of the socialist economic system reform, people's courts at all levels shall conduct thorough and systematic investigations and studies on new situations and new problems, grasp the situation, make specific analyses of specific circumstances, proceed from reality in everything, and handle matters properly and realistically.

(1) A large number of administrative cases are being brought to court. In accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations, the vast majority of administrative cases should first be handled by the competent administrative department. If a party is dissatisfied with the administrative handling or sanction, and if laws and regulations stipulate that a lawsuit may be filed in a people's court, the court shall accept the case immediately; if laws and regulations do not stipulate that a lawsuit may be filed in a people's court, pending any new or supplementary provisions by the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee or the State Council, the matter shall still be handled in accordance with the principle of Article 3, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

(2) Many internal economic disputes within enterprises are being brought to court. Such disputes should, in principle, be handled by the enterprise or its superior competent authority. Disputes over wages, welfare, bonuses, etc., due to differing circumstances in each unit and many changes, are more appropriately mediated by the enterprise or its superior competent authority. Most disputes over internal enterprise contracts should be mediated by the enterprise or its superior competent authority; only a very few that violate the law and must be accepted by a people's court shall be accepted by the people's court.

(3) The vast majority of rural contract disputes can be resolved through mediation by local grassroots organizations, relevant departments, and people's mediation committees. For those brought to a people's court, the people's court shall accept them according to law. Disputes over water rights, field boundaries, etc., are highly time-sensitive and should be promptly resolved through mediation by the relevant parties to facilitate production and prevent intensification of conflicts.

The above points should be closely monitored by people's courts at all levels regarding the development of the situation and the effects of handling, and experience should be summarized at any time, with better methods reported to this Court. In addition, for new situations and new problems not mentioned here, people's courts at all levels are requested to strengthen investigation and research and propose handling methods.

3. Strictly Adjudicate Cases According to Law and Improve the Quality of Adjudication

Since the Third Plenary Session of the Eleventh Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, there has been great development in socialist democracy and strengthening of the socialist legal system. National legislation, including economic legislation, has made significant progress. From 1979 to the present, the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee have adopted 45 important laws, 20 of which are important economic laws; they have also adopted 47 important resolutions and decisions. From 1979 to the end of October this year, the State Council formulated 422 administrative regulations, 317 of which are economic administrative regulations. In accordance with the "Decision on Authorizing the State Council to Formulate Interim Provisions or Regulations in the Area of Economic System Reform and Opening Up," adopted at the Third Session of the Sixth National People's Congress, the State Council will formulate more economic and administrative regulations in the coming period.

All judicial personnel of people's courts at all levels shall earnestly study, deeply research, correctly apply all the above laws and regulations, improve the quality of adjudication, and effectively ensure that laws are observed, enforcement is strict, and lawbreakers are prosecuted.

Article 100 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "The people's congresses of provinces and municipalities directly under the Central Government and their standing committees may, provided they do not contradict the Constitution, laws, and administrative regulations, formulate local regulations, which shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for the record." People's courts may use these local regulations as a basis, study them carefully, and correctly apply them when trying economic dispute cases belonging to the local area. If it is found that local regulations contradict the Constitution, laws, or administrative regulations, the matter shall be raised with the local people's congress and its standing committee.

Article 116 of the Constitution stipulates: "The people's congresses of national autonomous areas have the power to formulate autonomous regulations and separate regulations in accordance with the political, economic, and cultural characteristics of the local nationality. The autonomous regulations and separate regulations of autonomous regions shall take effect after being submitted to and approved by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The autonomous regulations and separate regulations of autonomous prefectures and autonomous counties shall take effect after being submitted to and approved by the standing committees of the people's congresses of the relevant provinces or autonomous regions, and shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for the record." People's courts may use these autonomous regulations and separate regulations of national autonomous areas as a basis, study them carefully, and correctly apply them when trying economic dispute cases belonging to the local national autonomous area.

When trying economic dispute cases, people's courts shall implement the principle of "emphasizing mediation" stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation); they shall summarize mediation work experience, and further improve the quality of mediation work. It must be ensured that the distinction between right and wrong is clear, responsibility is clear, and the process is lawful and voluntary; cases should not be delayed in mediation to the point of no conclusion; to protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties and safeguard the interests of the state and collectives.

4. Go Among the Masses to Resolve Economic Disputes

Judicial personnel of people's courts should pay attention to improving work methods and work style. They should not simply wait for cases to come in, handle cases in isolation, or work behind closed doors; they should carry forward the fine tradition of the mass line, go out of the office, enter factories, mines, enterprises, and institutions, go to the countryside, go among the masses, and actively provide judicial services. People's courts, through handling economic dispute cases, especially typical cases, should use the cases to explain the law, conduct vivid legal education for grassroots cadres and the masses, so that grassroots cadres and the masses know in economic activities: what is legal and what is illegal; what economic contracts are valid and what are invalid; what are false contracts; and know how to enter into economic contracts. In many localities, people's courts have adopted this method: handling one case, educating a whole area, and solving a series of problems, greatly reducing economic contract disputes, and enabling many grassroots cadres and the masses to learn how to mediate economic disputes themselves according to law. This experience should be widely promoted. Judicial personnel of people's courts should not only do a good job in adjudication but also do mass work; they should act both as judges and as legal propagandists.

5. Economic Adjudication Personnel Must Have Strict Discipline

People's courts at all levels shall strengthen education on communist ideals and discipline for their judicial personnel, resist and oppose the erosion of corrupt bourgeois and feudalist ideas, resist and oppose bourgeois liberalization ideas, and resist and oppose the influence of money-worship and individualism. People's judges are state law enforcement personnel who should serve the people wholeheartedly, safeguard the dignity of the law with every word and deed, and establish the authority of the socialist legal system. People's judges must be realistic and pragmatic, handle affairs according to law, be upright and impartial, and be incorruptible. People's judges, in trying economic cases and all other cases, must have strict discipline, abide by the law, and uphold public morality. It is absolutely not permitted for law enforcement personnel to violate the law. They are not allowed to pull strings, accept invitations for meals or gifts, or take advantage; still less are they allowed to accept bribes. Courts and court cadres are not allowed to engage in business activities. Court cadres are strictly prohibited from participating in illegal activities such as profiteering or buying shares and receiving dividends in economic units. Any act of violating law and discipline, bending the law for personal gain, or engaging in favoritism and fraud shall, once discovered, be severely punished. People's courts at all levels must seriously investigate and strictly handle any discovered illegal acts such as bribery, bending the law for personal gain, illegal business activities, and speculation, up to and including criminal prosecution according to law. Under no circumstances should they tolerate, cover up, or let the matter drop. Relevant information should be reported to this Court in a timely manner.

6. Strengthen Adjudication Forces and Improve Conditions for Handling Cases

People's courts at all levels shall further strengthen the forces of their economic adjudication divisions. If personnel must be increased, reasonable adjustments shall be made within the existing establishment; divisions with fewer cases should support divisions with more cases. The most important issue at present is to vigorously improve the quality of judicial personnel, enhance their political level, economic theory and policy level, and legal professional level. According to work needs, professional training courses may be organized, or cadres may be selected for professional training. At the same time, economic adjudication personnel should go deep into the practice of economic system reform, conduct investigation and research, learn and become familiar with the guiding ideology, basic principles and basic policies of economic system reform, as well as practical experience in reform. Special attention should be paid to analyzing and summarizing typical cases, summing up adjudication experience, and improving professional competence.

Economic dispute cases are generally complex and involve a wide range of areas. Many cases require investigation and evidence collection in many units and many locations, often requiring significant expenses. People's courts at all levels generally have insufficient funding for handling cases, especially grassroots people's courts. As a result, some cases cannot be completed midway due to insufficient funding; some grassroots people's courts have been forced to suspend acceptance of cases due to insufficient funding. To solve the problem of funding for handling cases, this Court, together with the Ministry of Finance, issued the "Notice on Effectively Solving the Difficulties in the Business Funding of People's Courts" on August 31, 1985. Courts at all levels should conduct investigation and research on funding for handling cases, grasp the actual needs, propose realistic budgets, and submit them to relevant departments for resolution.

If any new situations or problems arise during the implementation of the above notice, please report them to this Court in a timely manner.

December 9, 1985
